result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.single_target_shortest_path_length()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Find the shortest-path distance from every node to a target. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L46643-L46707){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.single_target_shortest_path_length( target, cutoff=None, weighted=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Single-target shortest path lengths](/assets/graphs/single-target-shortest-path-length.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The one-way street network shop to home to park to station. Each node shows its distance to the target station (outlined) in hops, shaded darker the closer it is: station 0, park 1, home 2, shop 3. The table lists the same distances." width="100%"} Like `single_target_shortest_path()` but returns only the distances: how far each node is from the target, following edge direction. Typical uses are "time to the nearest exit" or "hops to the sink" maps. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [target]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The destination node, as an ID or label. [cutoff]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional maximum distance; nodes farther away are left out. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to use edge weights. If `None` (default), follows the graph's `weighted` flag. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[int, int | float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : For every node that reaches `target`, its distance (`int` hops when unweighted). ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the target does not exist or a negative cycle can reach it. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} A single search over reversed edges. Matches NetworkX's `single_target_shortest_path_length`. ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#83407eb4 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec streets = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_nodes(["home", "park", "shop", "station"]) streets.add_edges([("home", "park"), ("park", "station"), ("shop", "home")]) lengths = streets.single_target_shortest_path_length("station") {streets.get_label_from_id(n): d for n, d in lengths.items()} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'home': 2, 'park': 1, 'shop': 3, 'station': 0} ``` ::: :::
